messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert — unusual auth traffic detected from a small set of IPs hitting the public inference proxy. Possible log spill reported by our log-collector. See brief: https://internal.re/redwood/alerts/3770001234
anya: I'm on call, pulling details now. Which customers are hitting the proxy?
mike: Confirmed spikes on /v1/generate and /v1/chat endpoints. Sample logs show repeated 401 then success with reused session tokens. snippet: `2026-03-17T10:05:12Z proxy-01 auth=401 ip=34.201.12.9 tok=anon_abc` then `2026-03-17T10:05:19Z proxy-01 auth=200 ip=34.201.12.9 tok=user_xxx`
kevin: That IP range resolves to cloud-provider IPs in eu-west-1. Could be a botnet testing creds.
jordan: Any customer-facing errors or reports?
anya: Not seeing customer tickets yet, but metrics show a small bump in failed auth for two enterprise accounts (acme-corp, blueocean). I flagged account owners.
secops: Possible sensitive logs leaked: the collector flagged S3 object /prod/proxy/logs/2026-03-17/proxy-01-10:05.gz for containing auth headers. Need to validate exposure window.
mike: I ran quick grep on the object: found header-like strings and partial bearer tokens. Might be truncated, but treat as PII/credentials.
kevin: Immediate actions: 1) rotate session signing key (short TTL) 2) invalidate active session tokens for impacted tenants 3) restrict proxy ingress to rate-limit those IPs. Who can rotate keys?
devops: I can push a rotation to staging quickly. For prod we need a hot-rotate plan — will coordinate with infra. Command to list current key: `rdwctl keys list --env prod`
anya: I'll take token invalidation for the two impacted customers. Running script now: `scripts/invalidate_sessions --tenant acme-corp,blueocean --reason "suspected leak 3770001234"`
jordan: I'll draft customer outreach templates. Prioritize clarity: what we know, what we're doing, ask them to rotate any app-level keys.
secops: Legal loop — @legal we need review for notification requirements, data exfiltration risk, and whether we must notify regulators.
legal: Acknowledge. Send me the list of potentially exposed identifiers and timeframe. We'll advise on notification cadence.
mike: Quick mitigation checklist I suggest: `1) apply source IP denylist on edge 2) enable stricter rate-limits for anonymous traffic 3) rotate session signing key 4) revoke affected sessions 5) snapshot and preserve logs for forensics`
devops: Applied temporary denylist for 34.201.12.0/24 via edge-control, propagated in 18s. :white_check_mark:
kevin: Prepping key rotation playbook: we'll generate a new signing key, deploy with dual-key acceptance window of 5 minutes, then retire old key. Need to communicate to dedicated customers if they pin tokens.
anya: Invalidation script finished for acme-corp and blueocean. Confirmed ~420 sessions revoked across regions.
jordan: Customer outreach sent to acme-corp lead, awaiting reply. I included steps for rotating their own API keys.
secops: Forensics job queued to clone the suspected S3 object and run deeper parsing — keeping backups of originals.
mike: One odd thing: our log forwarder to third-party-sys (log-analytics partner) showed a small burst between 10:04-10:07. I've paused forwarding to that integration until we confirm no exfil.
legal: Keep me updated. If third-party received raw auth headers, we likely have to notify affected customers and regulators.
anya: Handing off to next on-call @mike for overnight monitoring and follow-ups. Summary: suspect auth-probe -> possible log exposure -> rotated tokens for 2 tenants, denylisted IP range, paused forwarder, key rotation plan in progress.
mike: I'll monitor anomalies and coordinate with secops tomorrow AM. Setting a follow-up incident check at 2026-03-18T08:00Z.
secops: Adding case ticket: CASE-2026-3770001234. Forensics will add indicators and IOC list.
jordan: Thanks team. Will update customers as we confirm more. :pray:
incident-bot: Incident thread closed by oncall after handoff. Marked severity: high, status: mitigation in progress.
